과학기술정보통신부(장관 배경훈)는 한국기계연구원·한국전자통신연구원(ETRI)과 ‘AI 휴머노이드 데이터 팩토리’를 개소했다고 4일 밝혔다.

데이터 팩토리는 국내 최초의 이족보행 휴머노이드 전용 데이터 생산시설로 기계연구원이 ETRI와 협력해 구축했다. 기계연은 내년 말부터 산·학·연에 단계적으로 개방할 예정이다.

휴머노이드 12대가 운영되며 팔·다리 동작에서 전신 작업까지 다양한 데이터를 수집한다. 수집한 데이터는 AI 학습과 실제 로봇 검증을 반복하며 로봇의 자율 작업 성능을 높이는 데 활용한다는 방침이다.

김성수 과기정통부 연구개발정책실장은 “AI 휴머노이드 경쟁력 확보를 위해서는 공공 데이터 인프라 구축이 중요하다”며 “독자적인 AI 휴머노이드 기술 확보와 K-문샷 미션 달성에 총력을 다하겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
충청남도가 직장인 등 낮 시간대 교육 참여가 어려운 주민들을 위해 생성 AI 야간교육을 운영하고 있다고 4일 밝혔다.

충남은 지난 10월19일부터 아산장재우체국 내 AI디지털배움터 아산거점센터에서 지역 주민을 대상으로 ‘2026년 생성형 AI 이해와 활용’ 과정을 진행하고 있다. 총 8회에 걸쳐 생성 AI의 기본 원리부터 실생활과 업무에 활용하는 방법까지 실습 중심으로 교육한다.

주요 내용은 챗GPT와 제미나이 활용법, 이메일·안내문 작성, AI 이미지 제작, 긴 글 요약, 회의 내용 정리 등이다. 엑셀 활용과 발표자료·홍보자료 제작 방법도 다룬다. 교육생의 AI 활용 경험과 이해 수준에 따라 수업 진도를 조정하며, 실습에 어려움을 겪는 교육생에게는 보조강사가 개별 지도를 제공한다.

교육에 참여한 한 직장인은 "평소 업무에도 AI를 사용했지만 어떻게 하면 더 잘 활용할 수 있는지는 몰랐다"라며 "직장 때문에 낮에는 참여하기 어려웠는데 야간교육을 통해 모르던 기능과 활용법을 배울 수 있었다"라고 말했다.

충남은 앞으로도 주민들의 생활 패턴을 고려해 AI 교육 접근성을 높일 계획이다. 충남 AI디지털배움터 교육은 도내 모든 주민을 대상으로 운영하며, 참여 신청은 AI디지털배움터 공식 누리집에서 할 수 있다.

items.title: AMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in history
items.summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su said in the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that Q3 2026 was "was the largest and most profitable in our history." AMD reported a record $13.4 billion in quarterly revenue, and it's predicting it will hit another record high next quarter of $17 billio
items.content:
AMD thinks over 80 percent of its revenue will eventually come from its data center business alone.﻿

AMD CEO Lisa Su said in the company’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that Q3 2026 was “was the largest and most profitable in our history.” AMD reported a record $13.4 billion in quarterly revenue, and it’s predicting it will hit another record high next quarter of $17 billion. The company’s data center business is driving that growth, with $8.5 billion in data center quarterly revenue for Q3 2026. Su said AMD’s expecting its revenue to “grow more than 80 percent in 2027,” adding that “data center will be the largest contributor.”

Eventually, most of AMD’s revenue might come from its data center business. In response to a question during Tuesday’s earnings call, CFO Jean Hu said, “Looking ahead of 2027, we actually think our data center business will be more than 80 percent of total company revenue.”

As of Q3 2026, roughly 63 percent of AMD’s net quarterly revenue was from its data center business. Over the last couple years, jumps in the company’s revenue have been closely mirroring its data center business — in Q3 2026 its overall revenue went up $1.9 billion, while its data center revenue went up $1.8 billion.

As AMD keeps smashing its data center revenue records, its gaming business dropped 40 percent compared to last year, dipping to $773 million. PCs, game consoles, and other tech have been hit with price hikes over recent months due to shortages of RAM and other components, driven by demand from AI data centers. The shortage might not end anytime soon — Intel said it’s not expecting the shortage to improve next year, and SK Hynix predicted it’ll last until 2030 .

Su acknowledged the price hikes, saying, “Our view is, this is one of those times — when, you know, component prices go up, it affects overall system pricing. One would expect the consumer markets to be more sensitive to that, and so we have seen a bit of a slowdown in the sell-through.” Su added, “We are planning with the current environment for a down year for 2027.”

items.title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
items.summary: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare "whether AI has been used in their work," the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the plat
items.content:
Nexus Mods says that authors of newly uploaded mods will have to declare whether AI was ‘used in their work.’

The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare “whether AI has been used in their work,” the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform.

“One of the most consistent concerns we’ve heard is that it’s not clearly disclosed when AI has been used to create a mod,” according to the post from site owner Victor “Foledinho” Folmann. “We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognise that there’s a lot more we can do to make that information more accessible and clear for you all.” Any mods tagged as “AI-assisted” will also be required to include “a public explanation of how and where AI was used.” AI tags will also be “more prominent” on mod pages.

Folmann says Nexus Mods is “pro-human creativity” but “won’t introduce an outright ban on AI-generated mods.” As for why that is:

The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable. An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use. We’d prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform.

Folmann notes that Nexus Mods won’t use mods to train AI and “will not sell or license them to anyone doing so.” However, the site is working on “clearer control” over how mods can be reused on others and strengthening attribution for when “a mod uses another Mod Author’s mod with the appropriate permissions.”

Nexus Mods is also making changes to the Recently Added section of the site to address a problem of mod authors uploading many mods at once, which makes other mods fall down down the page. “This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up,” Folmann says. The changes include trying limits on how many mods from one author are shown at a time and “tighter restrictions” on uploads from new accounts. The platform is also launching controls to hide AI-generated content in game pages and on the homepage, and “next up,” in search.

Nexus Mods’ full AI policy is here , and mod authors have 60 days to update their existing mods to meet the requirements. The 60-day grace period ends on January 2nd, and after that time, the site will begin enforcing the rules.

items.content:
저자는 sLLM의 구축부터 배포까지 전 과정을 실습으로 안내하며, 개발자가 직접 맞춤형 AI를 만들고 운영하는 엔지니어로 성장하도록 돕습니다.

기업이 생성 AI를 들일 때 가장 먼저 걸리는 문턱은 여전히 데이터다. 메가존클라우드와 파운드리가 국내 기업 AI·IT 담당자 749명에게 물은 조사에서 생성형 AI의 주요 우려로 보안·개인정보 유출을 꼽은 응답은 53.3%였다. 자체 모델을 택한 기업이 꼽은 이유도 보안과 데이터 통제가 45.9%로 가장 많았다. 영풍문고 북마스터가 이번 주 고른 『원하는 대로 튜닝하는 나만의 sLLM』은 바로 이 지점에서 출발한다. 길벗이 지난 7월 7일 펴냈다.

책은 외부 대형 모델 대신 적은 연산 자원으로 돌릴 수 있는 소형 언어 모델(sLLM)을 사내에 직접 세우는 과정을 다룬다. 오픈소스 모델 선택과 데이터 전처리에서 시작해 풀 파인튜닝과 LoRA·QLoRA를 비교하고, 한국어 모델 파인튜닝을 실습한다. 이어 가지치기와 양자화, 지식 증류로 모델을 줄이고, KV 캐시와 플래시 어텐션 같은 추론 최적화, GPU 비용 절감까지 짚은 뒤 FastAPI와 Gradio로 서비스에 올린다. 예제는 무료 코랩 환경에서 그대로 돌아가도록 짰다.

모델을 만든 뒤의 쓰임새까지 이어지는 점도 눈에 띈다. 9장에서는 챗봇과 문서 요약 서비스, RAG 기반 AI 어시스턴트를 차례로 만들고, 랭체인과 라마인덱스로 문서 인덱싱과 쿼리 엔진을 붙인다. 한국어에 맞춘 모델을 우선 사용해 국내 실무 환경에 바로 옮겨 보기 쉽게 했고, 의료·공공·금융·법률 등 도메인별 활용 사례를 앞부분에 정리해 어느 업무부터 적용할지 가늠하게 돕는다.

영풍문고 매장에서도 비슷한 흐름이 읽힌다는 게 MD들의 전언이다. 이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD는 "프롬프트 활용서를 집던 손님 가운데 사내망에서 돌릴 수 있는 모델을 다룬 책이 있느냐고 묻는 경우가 생겼다"며 "그런 질문에 개념서가 아닌 실습서로 답할 수 있는 책"이라고 말했다.

권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 "앞부분 세 장은 시장 동향과 모델 소개라 실무자라면 4장 학습 환경부터 펼쳐도 된다"며 "10장의 데이터 부족과 출력 품질 문제 해결은 현장에서 바로 부딪히는 대목"이라고 덧붙였다.

저자 오지영은 컴퓨터공학 박사로 SK쉴더스와 GSITM을 거쳐 한국표준협회 AI융합추진단에서 AI·AX 사업전략을 맡고 있다. 기업과 공공 현장에서 AI를 시작조차 못 하는 조직을 자주 본 경험이 책을 쓴 계기라고 밝힌다. 영풍문고는 모델의 크기보다 쓰임새를 묻는 이 책이, 비용과 보안 사이에서 길을 찾는 엔지니어에게 든든한 출발점이 되리라 본다.

items.title: Please stop asking me when the AI bubble will pop
items.summary: People, including on this staff, keep asking me with varying degrees of excitement or trepidation when the AI bubble will burst. I'll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my
items.content:
I’m getting some real mixed messages here, boys!

People, including on this staff, keep asking me with varying degrees of excitement or trepidation when the AI bubble will burst. I’ll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my money, go retire on a beach somewhere. Maybe run a cat sanctuary, who knows.

What I can tell you is that I read with interest a story in Bloomberg this morning: “ Wall Street CEOs, Big Money Managers Divided Over AI Risks .” The story itself is a roundup of stuff said at the 2026 Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit in Hong Kong. Here’s what caught my attention: The CEO of Pacific Investment Management Co. — that’s PIMCO, the legendary bond firm — told listeners that there’s going to be a downturn in the AI market “and then things are going to break.”

“What we don’t know is how pricing and economics will evolve.”

The astronomically expensive AI buildout has swamped debt markets — making it harder to raise cash. But there’s still more debt coming, and people still want to buy it. For instance, Meta drew $58 billion in orders for a bond offering that’s expected to be $15 billion to $20 billion, Bloomberg reported today. Oracle said Monday it would need another $20 billion in bonds , on top of its existing steep commitments . Alphabet, Google’s parent company, is selling €6 billion (or about $6.7 billion) of bonds. Even Microsoft recently sold bonds , for the first time in a decade — $25 billion of them.

The PIMCO CEO — his name is Emmanuel Roman, but his job is what matters here — has estimated that the AI buildout could create $2 trillion in financing needs over the next five years. The entire total US bond market is about $12 trillion.

I am harping on PIMCO because it has been instrumental in the AI trade. It was among the group of financiers that did the first CoreWeave chip-based financing in 2023. It made a quick $2 billion in paper gains from $29 billion in Meta bonds , meant to support the AI buildout, last year. It bought $4 billion of SpaceX bonds last month. If PIMCO’s CEO is publicly sounding the alarm about a bubble popping, that’s a big deal — especially since the company just sold a bunch of its AI debt .

It’s not just PIMCO urging caution. Apollo Global Management, which lately had been talking with SpaceX about a $40 billion chip deal , is also warning of AI risk. Apollo president Jim Zelter told analysts today that while he expects society will use “dramatically more computing power in the future” and that AI is improving quickly, there is still significant uncertainty. “What we don’t know is how pricing and economics will evolve.”

The sheer volume of interest on Meta’s bonds suggests we are not at the top of the market. But there have been reports from China that its AI bubble burst some time ago. Meanwhile Wall Street banks were tripping over themselves to finance $63 billion in debt from Anthropic — not even a hyperscaler.

This is what I mean when I say “I don’t know.” I do think, though, that something major — PIMCO’s Roman singled out US rate hikes, war, or a eurozone crisis as potential triggers — could flip this market. We’re not in go-go-go territory now. Maybe that will change; it’s possible Anthropic’s IPO will go blockbuster and it’ll be like when someone rolls up to a party that’s running low on beer with a 24-pack. But as more people are expressing caution — and particularly after the disaster at Situational Awareness — the best part of the party might be over.

items.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
items.summary: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
items.content:
Anthropic is working on an open source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve , is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” — a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using.

Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results.

FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model. “A developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model,” the researchers write. “How can a user verify these claims?”

To work, the system requires AI labs to publish a “fingerprint” of each model they release that can later be matched to specific outputs and verified cryptographically. Crucially, the fingerprints don’t reveal a model’s weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private. That means labs could publish the fingerprints without giving up their most valuable asset, enabling the system to work with commercial models, too. The system is also designed to be lightweight, so verification could be performed on a local device.

As part of the announcement, researchers released a detailed technical specification and working code for various elements of the system, which is publicly available under an open source license on GitHub . Research in the system is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab.

“This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda,” researchers explain in the announcement post. “We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.”

매출 전년比 11% 증가에도 3분기 연속 영업손실…화재 손실 3540억원 반영

유통/생활/문화 입력 :2026/11/04 07:38 수정: 2026/11/04 08:35

쿠팡 미국 모회사인 쿠팡Inc가 올해 3분기 역대 최대 매출을 기록했지만, 6000억원이 넘는 영업손실을 내며 적자에서 벗어나지 못했다. 인천 물류센터 화재로 발생한 손실 약 3540억원이 반영된 데다 영업비용이 증가하면서 수익성이 악화됐다.

쿠팡Inc가3일(현지시간) 미국 증권거래위원회(SEC)에 제출한 3분기 연결실적 보고서에 따르면, 3분기 매출은 99억6200만 달러(약 14조2209억원)로 전년 동기(92억6700만 달러) 대비 7% 증가했다. 올해 3분기 평균 원·달러 환율인 1427.52원을 적용한 원화 기준 매출은 전년 동기 대비 11% 늘었다.

같은 기간 영업손실은 4억5000만 달러(약 6423억원)로, 전년 동기 영업이익 1억6200만 달러(약 2245억원)에서 적자 전환했다. 쿠팡은 올해 1분기 3545억원, 2분기 8350억원에 이어 3분기까지 3개 분기 연속 영업손실을 기록했다.

당기순손실도 5억100만 달러(약 7151억원)로 전년 동기 당기순이익 9500만 달러(약 1316억원)에서 적자로 돌아섰다. 올해 1분기 3897억원, 2분기 8560억원에 이어 3분기 연속 순손실이다. 주당순손실은 0.28달러로 집계됐다.

이번 실적에는 지난 7월 발생한 인천 물류센터 화재 손실이 반영됐다. 쿠팡Inc는 화재 관련 손실비용 2억4800만 달러(약 3540억원)를 3분기 실적에 반영했다고 밝혔다.

쿠팡Inc에 따르면 화재 손실을 제외한 3분기 영업손실은 2억200만 달러(약 2883억원)였을 것으로 추산된다. 당기순손실은 3억2100만 달러(약 4582억원) 수준이다. 화재 손실을 제외하더라도 적자를 기록한 셈이다.

앞서 쿠팡Inc는 지난 2분기 실적 발표에서 인천 물류센터 화재와 관련해 시설 보유 재고와 고정자산의 장부가치, 판매자 재고자산 관련 지급 의무 등을 합쳐 약 2억4600만 달러의 손실이 발생할 것으로 추산했다. 당시 회사는 관련 손실을 3분기부터 인식할 예정이라고 설명한 바 있다.

매출 증가에도 비용 부담은 커졌다. 3분기 매출원가는 74억100만 달러로 매출 대비 원가율이 74.3%를 기록했다. 이는 전년 동기(70.6%)보다 3.7%포인트 높아진 수치다.

판매비 및 관리비도 30억1100만 달러로 전년 동기(25억5800만 달러) 대비 17.7% 증가했다. 이에 따라 총 영업비용은 104억1200만 달러로 매출을 웃돌았다.

매출총이익은 25억6100만 달러로 전년 동기 대비 6% 감소했다. 조정 상각 전 영업이익(EBITDA)은 1억1600만 달러로 전년 동기(4억1300만 달러)보다 72% 줄었다.

핵심 사업인 프로덕트 커머스 부문은 성장세를 이어갔지만 수익성은 악화됐다.

로켓배송과 로켓프레시, 로켓그로스, 마켓플레이스 등을 포함한 프로덕트 커머스 부문의 3분기 매출은 83억7400만 달러(약 11조9540억원)로 전년 동기 대비 달러 기준 5%, 원화 기준 8% 증가했다.

반면 이 부문의 조정 EBITDA는 3억8500만 달러(약 5495억원)로 전년 동기(7억500만 달러) 대비 45% 감소했다. 조정 EBITDA 마진율은 4.6%를 기록했다.

고객 수와 고객당 매출은 모두 증가했다. 3분기 프로덕트 커머스 활성고객은 2520만명으로 전년 동기(2470만명) 대비 2% 늘었다. 직전 분기인 올해 2분기와 비교해도 50만명 증가했다.

활성고객 1인당 매출은 332달러(약 47만3930원)로 전년 동기 323달러(약 44만7730원)보다 원화 기준 6% 증가했다.

대만 로켓배송과 파페치, 쿠팡이츠 등이 포함된 성장사업 부문 매출은 15억8800만 달러(약 2조2669억원)로 전년 동기(12억8700만 달러) 대비 23% 증가했다. 고정환율 기준 성장률은 27%다.

성장사업 부문의 조정 EBITDA 손실은 2억6900만 달러(약 3840억원)로 전년 동기(2억9200만 달러)보다 소폭 줄었다. 해외 사업 등에 대한 투자가 이어지는 가운데 손실 규모는 다소 축소된 것으로 나타났다.

서비스 기획·개발·인프라 등 7개 분야 모집…내달 최종 합격자 발표

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/11/04 07:21

정부가 대국민 인공지능(AI) 서비스 개발에 속도를 내기 위해 민간 전문가를 추가 채용한다.

과학기술정보통신부는 국민AI서비스혁신추진단에서 AI 서비스 개발을 담당할 전문임기제 공무원 19명을 추가로 공개 모집한다고 3일 밝혔다. 지난 9월 1차 모집에 이은 두 번째 채용으로 서비스 기획·개발·인프라·보안 등 7개 분야에서 인력을 선발한다.

추진단은 기존 외주 중심 개발 방식과 달리 민간 개발자와 공무원이 함께 서비스를 직접 개발하는 조직이다. 임기제 공무원으로 채용된 민간 개발자와 'AI챔피언' 과정을 수료한 공무원이 국민 수요를 발굴하고 개발을 맡는다. AI챔피언은 공공부문 AI 전환을 이끌 실무 전문가를 양성·인증하는 프로그램이다.

이번 채용은 김세웅 전 카카오 AI 시너지 부사장이 지난 2일 추진단장으로 취임한 뒤 처음 진행하는 채용이다. 추진단은 전문인력을 추가 확보해 공공 AI 에이전트 등 대국민 서비스 개발 역량을 강화할 계획이다.

채용 직급은 전문임기제 가·나·다급이며 임기는 채용일부터 2028년 9월 30일까지다. 채용 공고는 지난 2일부터 게시됐으며 원서 접수는 오는 10일부터 12일까지 진행한다.

전형은 서류심사와 면접 순으로 진행하며 최종 합격자는 12월 중 발표할 예정이다. 분야별 모집 인원과 자격 요건 및 근무조건은 과기정통부 홈페이지와 나라일터에 게시된 공고문에서 확인할 수 있다.

김세웅 국민AI서비스혁신추진단장은 "국민이 일상에서 겪는 불편을 AI로 실제로 해결하려면 현장을 이해하고 빠르게 만들어 낼 수 있는 개발자가 핵심"이라며 "민간 속도와 공공 책임성을 결합해 국민에게 실질적인 도움이 되는 서비스를 함께 만들어 갈 역량 있는 인재들의 많은 지원을 바란다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
Early access testing for the Sonos AI voice assistant is right around the corner.

Sonos is rolling out a big app update that includes new Presets and early access to its AI voice assistant. You can create a preset to play music at a specific volume in a certain room, which will appear directly on the homescreen so you can quickly start playback.

As teased by Sonos previously, you’ll be able to use the assistant to do things like start music, move playback to another room, group and ungroup speakers, and set timers. But Sonos says it can also complete more complicated requests using natural language, such as “Play the album with a sardine tin on the cover,” or “Who was the singer at the superbowl? Play their latest album on Hallway.”

These updates are part of efforts to recover from a disastrous app redesign in 2024, which Sonos CEO Tom Conrad has promised to reverse . The company launched a revamped Sonos 27 app operating system update in September with the ability to connect AI agents to the app. Sonos plans to allow users to create up to 10 custom agents as well.

Other features coming to the Sonos app in this update include the ability to swipe on the “Now Playing” screen or mini player to skip tracks, and a way to rearrange your favorites. The Sonos app can also work with the iOS-only System Health feature, which can help you spot problems in your setup.

지디넷코리아가 소프트웨어(SW) 업계의 다양한 소식을 한눈에 볼 수 있는 'ZD SW 투데이'를 마련했습니다. SW뿐 아니라 클라우드, 보안, 인공지능(AI) 등 여러 분야에서 활발히 활동하고 있는 기업들의 소식을 담은 만큼 좀 더 쉽고 편하게 이슈를 확인해 보시기 바랍니다. [편집자주]

■미소정보기술, 의료AX·기기 산업화

미소정보기술이 연세대 원주 연세의료원, 원주의료기기산업진흥원(WMIT)과 의료 AI·의료기기 산업의 사업화 촉진을 위한 '의료AX 및 의료기기 산업화 패스트트랙' 업무협약을 체결했다.

이번 협약은 3개 기관이 보유한 의료기관의 임상 인프라, 산업지원기관의 기업 육성 역량, AI·데이터 전문기업 기술력을 유기적으로 결합해 의료 AI·디지털헬스 제품 실증부터 임상시험, 인허가, 보험등재, 시장 진입까지 전 과정을 지원하는 개방형 산업화 협력체계를 구축하기 위해 마련됐다.

특히 AI 의료기기 산업화의 핵심 요소로 부상하고 있는 실사용근거(RWE) 창출 기능을 병원 내 공공형 임상시험수탁기관 체계와 연계해 차별화된 원스톱 지원 모델을 구축할 계획이다. 이를 통해 의료 AI·디지털헬스 기업의 개발 초기 단계부터 임상 전문의 매칭, 임상시험 설계·수행, 실증 데이터 확보 등 임상시험 전반에 걸친 패키지형 지원을 제공하고 제품 신뢰성 확보와 인허가, 보험등재·시장 진출까지 이어지는 실질적인 사업화를 적극 지원할 방침이다.

■KDCC, AI 시대 데이터센터 탄소중립 실현 위한 세미나 개최

한국데이터센터연합회(KDCC)가 오는 10일 오후 2시 서울시 강남구에서 AI 시대 데이터센터의 탄소중립 세미나'를 개최한다.

이번 세미나는 데이터센터 탄소중립 관련 기술과 정책 동향을 공유하고, 산업 현장에서 활용할 수 있는 대응 전략을 모색하는 자리로 마련됐다.

KDCC는 올해부터 참여 중인 '탄소 인지디지털 서비스 인프라 아기텍처 및 통합 운영 기술개발' 연구개발과제의일환으로 AI 기술 확산에 따른 데이터센터 산업 성장과 에너지 수요 증가에 대응하고, 데이터센터 산업의 지속가능한 발전 방향을 모색하고 있다.

CJ올리브네트웍스가 운영하는 라이프스타일 멤버십 CJ원이 CJ더마켓·이마트24 할인 혜택을 제공하는 11월 '원더위크'를 개최한다.

CJ원은 7월부터 매월 회원 대상 '놀랍도록 훌륭한 혜택'을 선보이는 프로모션인 원더 시리즈를 진행하고 있다. 뚜레쥬르, 메가MGC커피 등 제휴 브랜드 협업을 통한 생활 밀착형 혜택으로 약 4개월간 월 평균 10만여 명의 신규 회원을 확보하고, 쿠폰 누적 다운로드 43만 회를 넘기는 등 인기를 얻고 있다.

11월 10일까지 진행하는 원더위크는 CJ제일제당 공식 자사몰 CJ더마켓에서 사용 가능한 쿠폰을 지급한다. CJ더마켓의 월간 할인 행사 '더마켓 세일 페스타(더세페)'와 연계했다. CJ원 앱에서 5일까지 프로모션 오픈 알림 신청 시, CJ더마켓 적립금 쿠폰(1천 원·3천 원·1만 원 중 1종) 또는 CJ원 포인트 중 한 가지를 랜덤으로 받을 수 있다.

■링크플로우, 코스닥 기술특례상장 기술성 평가 통과

링크플로우가 '온디바이스 AI 웨어러블 카메라' 기술로 코스닥 기술특례상장을 위한 기술성 평가를 통과했다.

링크플로우는 2016년 삼성전자 사내벤처 프로그램 씨랩에서 스핀오프해 설립된 온디바이스 AI 카메라·영상 솔루션 기업이다. 넥밴드형 카메라 FITT360, NEXX360을 시작으로 체스트형 바디캠 P3000, P3000A 등 다양한 착용 형태의 제품군을 구축해 왔다.

링크플로우는 이번 평가를 통해 온디바이스 AI 웨어러블 카메라 기술의 경쟁력과 사업화 가능성을 인정받았으며, 최종 상장을 위한 준비에도 박차를 가할 계획이다.

■엔티큐코리아, 티플리스와 AICC 사업 협력

엔티큐코리아가 콜센터·AI 컨택센터(AICC) 기업 티플리스와 손잡고 한국 AICC 시장에서 기술 협력과 신규 사업을 확대한다.

이번 협약은 두 기업 기술 역량과 산업 경험을 바탕으로 AICC 솔루션 개발, 시스템 구축, 프로젝트 수행 분야의 협력 체계를 마련하고 한국 시장에서 신규 사업 기회를 함께 발굴하기 위해 추진됐다.

370만명 관련 임금협상 난항…셰플러, 앞선 구조조정 끝내자 추가 감원

국내외 자동차·배터리 산업의 흐름을 읽는 시간. '세계車트'는 글로벌 완성차·배터리 업계의 주요 소식과 시장 변화, 기술 트렌드를 외신을 통해 짚어봅니다. [편집자주]

독일 자동차산업이 수요 부진과 비용 부담 속에 파업과 구조조정으로 흔들리고 있다. 노동자들은 임금 인상과 고용 보장을 요구하고 있지만, 기업들은 경쟁력 유지를 위해 인력을 더 줄여야 한다는 입장이다.

아우디·벤츠 파업…"임금 5% 인상·일자리 보장"

블룸버그통신에 따르면 자동차·기계·전기전자 등 독일 제조업 노동자를 대표하는 금속노조 IG메탈은 약 370만명의 근로자가 관련된 임금 협상에서 12개월간 임금 5% 인상과 일자리·생산거점 보호를 요구하고 있다. 10월 말 쟁의행위를 제한하는 기간이 끝나면서 아우디와 메르세데스벤츠, 셰플러 등에서 파업이 이어졌다.

사용자 측은 2027년 연간 세전 급여 1%를 일시금으로 지급하고, 2028년 7월부터 임금을 1.3% 인상하는 방안을 제시했다. 노조 요구와 차이가 큰 데다 사용자 측은 노동비용을 낮추지 못하면 추가 감원이 불가피하다고 경고했다.

아우디에서는 미국 투자 계획도 갈등의 배경이 됐다. 게르노트 될너 최고경영자(CEO)가 트럼프 미국 대통령의 선거 유세 행사에서 첫 미국 공장 건설 계획을 발표하자, 노조는 독일 사업장의 장기적인 고용 보장을 요구했다.

구조조정 끝내자 또 감원…車 부품사 셰플러, 3460명 줄인다

독일 자동차 부품업체 셰플러는 유럽 사업장 5곳을 폐쇄하고 3460명을 감원할 계획이라고 밝혔다. 폐쇄 대상은 독일 4곳과 벨기에 1곳이며, 감원 인원 약 75%가 독일에 집중된다. 앞서 유럽에서 4700명을 줄이는 구조조정을 조기 완료했다고 발표한 지 불과 몇 주 만이다.

회사는 내연기관차 수요 감소와 전기차 사업 확대 지연으로 생산량이 예상보다 빠르게 줄고 있다고 설명했다. 독일의 직원 1인당 비용이 다른 유럽 지역 약 2.5배에 달한다는 점도 감원 배경으로 들었다.

최고경영진은 기본급의 10%를 반납하고 관리조직도 두 단계 축소한다. 셰플러는 이번 조치로 2030년부터 연간 약 3억 유로를 절감할 것으로 예상했다. 반면 IG메탈과 그룹 사업장평의회는 반복되는 감원과 사업장 폐쇄가 독일 산업 기반을 약화한다며 반발했다.

items.title: Valve is making changes to deal with a ‘significant increase’ in Steam game submissions
items.summary: In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it's seen "a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months" and says it's "running a little behind" by taking "up to 12 business days" for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days. Indie developers have
items.content:
Valve admits that it’s now taking ‘up to 12 business days’ to review games.

In a new post today , Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days.

Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates . Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.”

The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes. “Believe it or not, sometimes we review builds that have not ever been played through Steam,” Valve says. “This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.”

Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install.

Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

items.title: Binance says hackers used fake job interviews and an internal AI tool to pull off the $6.3 billion heist
items.summary: The largest crypto theft to date was pulled off by combining some well-known hacking techniques over the course of a few months, according to Binance. A postmortem from the company says the process started in June with one developer downloading a tampered installer apparently spr
items.content:
A North Korean hacking unit reportedly started its break-in with a search engine ad that served up a malware download.

The l argest crypto theft to date was pulled off by combining some well-known hacking techniques over the course of a few months, according to Binance . A postmortem from the company says the process started in June with one developer downloading a tampered installer apparently spread by a malicious Google ad, exposing details about the engineers and how they work. Then, in September, another engineer was targeted by someone pretending to be interested in hiring them; that person set up a series of calls and multiple rounds of interviews, shared social media pages to build trust, and eventually prompted them to download a fake interview assignment that was actually malware.

Binance claims that its security teams did detect the first installation of malware in June, and replaced the worker’s device, but that its security tools didn’t detect the second attack that deleted the pyenv executable and replaced it with a malicious version that gave them backdoor access:

The malware employed sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The 0-day malware was not detected by the endpoint security protection tools at the time. The attacker also took steps to conceal the malicious activity and remove traces of the compromise, making detection and subsequent investigation more challenging.

By October 20th, the story goes, the attackers, whom the FBI has identified as a North Korean unit dubbed “TraderTraitor,” used Binance’s own internal AI tool to gain control over wallets for the first engineer compromised in June, as well as a third employee, before logging into the third employee’s computer on October 29th and launching their attack.

The postmortem also goes into why Binance wasn’t able to stop the transactions that occurred nearly two hours after the first unauthorized transfers, saying that “Because the hot wallet used Multi-Party Computation (MPC), there was no single private key that could be used to immediately revoke the malicious EIP-7702 authorizations.” Binance says that it has prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases, and CEO Richard Teng writes that no user is bearing the loss, with about $2.85 billion in stolen assets frozen or intercepted: “At this moment, 98% of impacted tokens had been replenished; we’re completing the remaining 2%. Withdrawals have broadly resumed.”

What’s less clear is why this particular attack worked — the danger of job interviews that ask people to download and execute code on machines with access to employer material has been warned about for years, and there’s little detail on the “internal AI tool” that was used by the attackers and why it was able to help them in the first place.

items.content:
최첨단 AI 모델들이 실제 기업의 전문 업무를 재현한 평가에서 최고 12%에 그쳤습니다. 기존 벤치마크가 실제 업무의 복잡성과 전문가의 판단 과정을 충분히 반영하지 못한다는 지적과 함께, AI가 기업의 고부가가치 전문 업무를 얼마나 완수할 수 있는지 측정하는 새로운 평가 방식이 등장했습니다.

반도체·AI 산업 분석 전문 세미애널리시스(SemiAnalysis)는 2일(현지시간) 새로운 AI 에이전트 벤치마크인 ' GDPx '를 공개했습니다. 반도체 설계, 사이버보안, 생물학, 금융, 법률, 소프트웨어 개발, AI 자기 개선(RSI) 등 11개 전문 분야에서 206개 작업을 수행하도록 했습니다. 이를 위해 전문 업체 14곳과 협력해 실제 업무 환경을 재현했습니다.

평가 결과, 앤트로픽의 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'가 12.0%로 1위를 차지했습니다. 구글의 '제미나이 4 카본'이 10.9%, 오픈AI의 'GPT-6 아스트라'가 9.6%, 메타의 '뮤즈 원더 풀'이 9.0%로 뒤를 이었습니다.

12%란 수치는 실제 업무 100개 중 12개를 완수했다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 과제별 완전 성공 여부와 부분 점수를 반영한 종합 점수입니다. 각 작업에 최대 8시간을 부여하고 세 차례 실행한 성적을 평균했습니다.

중요한 것은 세미애널리시스가 GDPx를 개발한 목적이 AI의 종합적인 지능 측정보다 실제 산업에서 경제적 가치를 창출할 수 있는 능력을 측정하는 데 있다는 것입니다. AI 도입으로 발생하는 초기 매출이 모든 직종에서 고르게 발생하기보다는 자동화 효과가 큰 일부 전문 산업에 집중될 것이라는 판단에서입니다.

이에 따라 전체 직업의 분포나 국내총생산(GDP) 비중 대신 반도체 설계, 금융, 사이버보안, AI 자기 개선 등 고부가가치 분야를 평가 대상으로 선정했습니다. 이번 평가 결과는 2027~2028년 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 매출을 예측하는 자체 분석에도 활용할 계획입니다.

이 과정에서 기존 실무 평가의 한계도 지적했습니다. 특히 지난해 9월 오픈AI가 공개한 'GDPval'을 사례로 들었습니다. GDPval도 실제 직업에서 수행하는 업무를 평가하지만, 필요한 자료와 지시를 미리 제공한 뒤 보고서나 결과물을 작성하도록 하는 방식에 치중했다는 것입니다. 실제 전문가는 수많은 자료에서 필요한 정보를 직접 찾고, 서로 충돌하는 내용을 비교하며, 명확하게 지시받지 않은 조건까지 판단해야 합니다. 세미애널리시스는 GDPval이 공개 당시에는 획기적인 평가였지만, AI 에이전트가 발전한 현재에는 이러한 능력을 충분히 측정하기 어렵다고 평가했습니다.

기존 벤치마크의 채점 방식에도 문제를 제기했습니다. 일부 평가에서 정답이 잘못 설정됐거나 올바른 해결책을 제출했는데도 오답으로 처리하는 사례가 있다고 지적했습니다. 자체 품질 검증 시스템을 '터미널 벤치 4.0'에 적용한 결과, 전체 과제의 약 50%에서 문제가 발견됐다고 주장했습니다. AI가 문제를 제대로 해결해도 특정 방식으로 답하지 않았다는 이유로 점수를 받지 못할 수 있다는 것입니다.

GDPx는 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 실제 업무 자료와 프로그램을 포함한 환경을 구축하고, 과제와 채점 기준의 오류까지 검증하도록 설계했습니다. 대표적인 금융 과제에서는 실제 기업 인수 거래를 바탕으로 약 4000개의 익명화된 파일을 포함한 가상 업무 환경을 만들었습니다. AI는 필요한 재무제표와 계약서, 회계자료 등을 직접 찾아 분석하고 기존 문서의 오류를 수정해야 했습니다. 단순히 정리된 자료를 바탕으로 답을 작성하는 것과는 다른 작업입니다.

실제 평가에서 AI 모델들은 복잡한 업무를 끝까지 완수하지 못하는 사례가 많았습니다. 기업의 수익성을 분석하는 한 금융 과제에서는 25차례 실행 가운데 완전히 성공한 사례가 없었습니다. 가장 높은 성적을 거둔 실행도 11개 검증 항목 중 8개만 통과했습니다. 계약 조건과 회계처리 기준을 종합적으로 판단하는 과정에서 실수를 보였습니다. 법률 분야에서도 투자계약 문서를 수정하는 과제에 4개 모델이 총 20차례 도전했지만 모두 완성 기준을 충족하지 못했습니다. 계약상 허점을 놓치거나 기존 합의와 충돌하는 조건을 추가하는 등의 오류가 나타났습니다.

종합 순위와 전문 분야별 성적이 일치하지 않았다는 점도 눈에 띕니다. 오퍼스 5.5는 반도체 설계와 하드웨어 설계, 퀀트 트레이딩에서 가장 높은 점수를 기록했습니다. 제미나이 4 카본은 생물학과 소프트웨어 개발, GPT-6 아스트라는 AI 자기 개선과 재료과학 분야에서 각각 1위를 차지했습니다. 종합 성능이 높은 모델도 모든 전문 분야에서 우수한 것은 아니라는 의미입니다.

그렇다고 기존 AI 벤치마크가 실제 업무를 다루지 않았던 것은 아닙니다. 대표적인 AI 평가업체 아티피셜 애널리시스(AA)도 최근 종합 지능 지수를 개편하면서 'AA 브리프케이스(AA-Briefcase)'와 '프론티어코드 2.0(FrontierCode 2.0)' 등 복잡한 업무 수행 능력을 측정하는 평가를 도입했습니다. GDPx는 이러한 흐름에서 특정 산업의 전문성과 경제적 활용 가능성에 집중했다는 차이가 있습니다. 따라서 GDPx의 낮은 점수를 기존 종합 지수와 직접 비교해 AI 성능이 떨어졌다고 해석할 수는 없습니다.

평가 결과 자체에도 한계는 있습니다. 모델마다 클로드 코드, 코덱스 등 서로 다른 에이전트 실행 환경을 사용했으며, 일부 사이버보안과 생물학 과제에서는 안전장치가 작업을 제한했습니다. 일부 과제의 세부 내용과 채점 기준이 공개되지 않아 외부에서 전체 결과를 독립적으로 재현하기도 어렵습니다.

이번 GDPx는 AI 벤치마크가 실제 업무 수행 능력을 측정하는 데서 나아가 산업별 전문성과 경제적 활용 가치를 검증하는 방향으로 바뀌고 있음을 보여줍니다. 특히 종합 성능이 뛰어난 모델도 모든 전문 분야에서 우수한 것은 아니며, 어려운 문제를 해결하는 능력과 복잡한 업무를 끝까지 완수하는 능력에도 차이가 있었습니다.

AI 에이전트의 산업 현장 도입이 늘면서 이러한 차이를 측정하는 전문 벤치마크도 세분될 것으로 보입니다.

■ 미소스 5.5·GPT-6.2 아스트라 잇달아 포착…최첨단 모델 출시설

앤트로픽 공식 웹사이트에서 '클로드 미소스 5.5'라는 이름이 발견되고, 오픈AI의 'GPT-6.2 아스트라'를 테스트하고 있다는 개발자들의 주장이 나왔습니다. 최근 최첨단 AI 모델에 대한 관심이 높아지면서 출시 전 새로운 모델의 흔적이나 유출 정황도 이전보다 큰 주목을 받는 모습입니다.

■ 구글, '제미나이 4 카본' 공개 사흘 만에 개선판 포착…3D 성능 호평

'제미나이 4 카본'이 공개된 지 사흘 만에 개선 버전인 '카본-H'가 AI 평가 플랫폼에서 테스트 중인 정황이 포착됐습니다. 전작에서 약점으로 지적됐던 3D 모델링과 디자인 성능이 뚜렷한 발전을 이뤘다는 평가가 나왔습니다.

■ "AI 50개 모아 문명 건설 시켰더니 관료주의에 빠져 실패"

에이전트 50개가 5900개의 메시지를 주고받으며 복잡한 역할 분담과 승인 절차에 매달리다가 마인크래프트 문명 건설에 실패했다는 실험 결과입니다. 여러 AI 에이전트가 실제 업무에서 협업할 때도 불필요한 의사결정과 절차에 빠져 생산성을 떨어뜨릴 수 있다는 점을 보여줬습니다.

items.title: Ted Schlein’s Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for new funds amid AI-driven cybersecurity boom
items.summary: Cybersecurity-focused Ballistic Ventures is seeking to raise $360 million for a new flagship fund and another $130 million for a separate investment vehicle.
items.content:
Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings.

The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing.

The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them.

Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah, and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault. The firm has backed companies, including Talon Cyber Security, acquired by Palo Alto Networks , and Pangea, bought by CrowdStrike , alongside startups such as Armadin , GetReal , Nudge Security, and Oligo Security.

Ballistic’s ties to storied venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins, where Schlein spent more than two decades, help set it apart from rivals, a cybersecurity investor at another VC firm told TechCrunch. Its investment strategy, however, is similar to those of other cybersecurity-focused investors, including Forgepoint Capital and Ten Eleven Ventures, the person said.

In 2022, Ballistic announced its $300 million debut fund and raised another $360 million for its second flagship fund two years later. It also raised about $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, per PitchBook data. The new Fund B is targeting a similar amount.

U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5 billion in 2025, the highest since 2022, a recent report by JPMorgan Chase said, citing PitchBook data. AI-enabled companies accounted for about 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May this year, compared with 36% in 2019, the report said.

Separately, Microsoft, in its annual Digital Defense Report released last month, warned that hackers are increasingly using AI for activities ranging from phishing and social engineering to malware development. The technology is allowing attackers to operate faster and at greater scale, even as many of their underlying techniques remain unchanged.

Ballistic Ventures declined to comment on its fundraising plans.

items.title: Safari introduces Adaptive Dark Mode in 27.3
items.summary: Article URL: https://webkit.org/blog/18541/introducing-adaptive-dark-mode/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50358562 Points: 317 # Comments: 189
items.content:
by Simon Fraser, Luming Yin, Lily Spiniolas, Joanne Pan, Veda Periwal and Jen Simmons

We’re excited to announce Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari 27.3 beta. When enabled by a user, Safari adapts light websites and presents them as dark.

In the spring of 2019, Safari 12.1 became the first browser to support dark mode on the web. A lot of people love using dark mode, but not every website has a dark version. Almost 40% of web page loads are from users in dark mode, and yet only 10% of page loads support it. If you love dark mode, you’ve probably hit a site that felt particularly bright . Adaptive Dark Mode is designed to close that gap, providing a consistent dark experience across the web.

You can try it today in Safari 27.3 beta. To enable, first make sure your system appearance is set to dark. Then browse to a website with a bright background. Safari will offer a preview of Adaptive Dark Mode. Tap ‘Try’.

For websites that signal support of dark mode with <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> in HTML or color-scheme: light dark in CSS, Adaptive Dark Mode does not change a thing. For the rest of the web, it quickly analyzes the page, looking at colors and estimating whether it’s predominantly light or dark. If the page generally has a dark background with light text, nothing is changed. When a page has a light appearance, Adaptive Dark Mode adapts the page to be dark.

At the core of Adaptive Dark Mode is the transformation of color. Sometimes colors are simply decorative, while other times they have semantic meaning. Adaptive Dark Mode determines when to invert colors so elements remain visible or when to leave colors unchanged.

While creating Adaptive Dark Mode, we developed a color matrix to invert the luminosity of colors while preserving hue. It’s used to make light backgrounds dark, and dark text light. When transforming text color, Adaptive Dark Mode aims for sufficient contrast as defined by the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio . Light CSS gradients are also transformed to dark.

Adaptive Dark Mode makes careful judgments so transformed content looks good and stays usable: buttons have contrast against backgrounds, text is visible over images, and hover menus look clear.

It takes the same care with images. Most are left unchanged, preserving their integrity. But many icons and logos can lose contrast when the background color behind them is inverted. So Adaptive Dark Mode inspects SVG images and transforms colors when needed. For bitmap images, it analyzes the pixel histograms and inverts simple black-and-white logos.

Effects like masks and mix-blend-mode can create undesirable results on an element whose colors have been transformed, so in some cases Adaptive Dark Mode turns such effects off. Also, <canvas> content is left unchanged, since canvases contain a wide range of content that’s hard to predict.

It’s precisely because Adaptive Dark Mode is happening deep within the WebKit browser engine that we are able to find creative ways to solve the most complex challenges, apply the transformations with great speed and power efficiency, all while rigorously protecting user privacy.

In general, a web page will work well with Adaptive Dark Mode if it follows good modern web development practices.

If your site still uses older techniques, small updates can help. For logos and icons, swap bitmap images for SVG. Use solid or gradient colors in CSS instead of tiled background images. Replace image sprites with modern CSS for rounded corners, shadows, and button states. Create content images with transparent backgrounds instead of baking the page background color into the image. Add padding to containers to prevent crowding.

Perhaps you want a specific dark mode experience for a certain portion of the page. Apply color-scheme: light dark to the relevant element and add your own dark styles.

For complete control over how your site looks in dark mode, add full support. It’s a terrific time to do so. It’s never been easier.

All the web technology needed to fully support dark mode is widely available today, including:

Newer CSS functions like color-mix() and contrast-color() , plus popular techniques for organizing design systems with CSS variables provide additional options and flexibility.

Be sure to declare dark mode support using the color-scheme meta tag in your HTML head and/or by setting the color-scheme property on :root or body in your CSS. Don’t wait to inject this information later via JavaScript. This best practice helps ensure your site is rendered correctly as fast as possible.

If you would like your web app or website to not be transformed by Adaptive Dark Mode, you can communicate this using color-scheme . The HTML <meta name="color-scheme" content="light only"> tag lets browsers know that 1) this page supports light mode and 2) should only be displayed in light mode. The color-scheme: light only rule does the same thing, but with the flexibility of CSS, allowing you to just target specific elements on the page — or of course, you can target the whole page with :root { } . (Note: the ‘only’ keyword is not supported in Safari 27.3 beta 1. Check back as Adaptive Dark Mode evolves through the beta process.)

Apple firmly believes user privacy is a fundamental human right. If websites could detect when a user has enabled Adaptive Dark Mode, that would increase the amount of fingerprintable information and weaken privacy protections against trackers.

As a result, Safari prevents websites from detecting when Adaptive Dark Mode has been applied. JavaScript that queries CSS colors will get the original authored colors, not the transformed ones. Any images drawn into canvas render in their original form.

If you manage a website or web app, and would like to discuss how Adaptive Dark Mode is adapting your project, feel free to reach out at web-evangelist@apple.com .

items.title: Here’s what it’s like to use Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch
items.summary: It's impossible to paint a full picture of what Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 will be right now. The watchOS 27.3 developer beta just dropped earlier this afternoon, and these features are meant to be lived with in day-to-day life. We're definitely g
items.content:
The watchOS 27.3 beta adds Live Rewind and Siri Recap to the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.

It’s impossible to paint a full picture of what Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 will be right now. The watchOS 27.3 developer beta just dropped earlier this afternoon, and these features are meant to be lived with in day-to-day life. We’re definitely going to do that over the next few weeks at The Verge . That said, here are some initial impressions.

What’s newly available today is Live Rewind and Siri Recap. The former lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds, while the latter provides high-level summaries of your conversations. (The other two Audio Intelligence features have been available for the last few weeks. I wrote about those in my Series 12 review .) And as always, this is the developer beta. These features could still change quite a bit before a final version arrives for the public.

The first thing I noticed is that these features are not turned on by default. I wasn’t expecting anything different, but it’s worth remembering that these features don’t automatically turn every Apple Watch into a surveillance device. Audio Intelligence requires the latest Apple Watch hardware, a compatible version of iOS (so in this case, the iOS 27.3 developer beta), and someone has to actively choose to enable these features. You can download the beta and double-press the crown to initiate a Live Rewind. It won’t do anything. You must opt in via your iPhone’s Watch app. Same goes for Siri Recap. Enabling Live Rewind also requires an initial microphone calibration with your phone.

Privacy-wise, Apple has publicly available support documentation about its approach to these features. I’m not weighing in on how well it executes them in this hands-on. But Apple has pretty clear messaging in the onboarding process. There are quite a few customization options for when Siri Recap is active. You can get pretty granular. For example, you can have Siri Recap on only at the office during weekdays from 1PM to 4PM if that’s when you have meetings. This is hard to convey to bystanders, and I think ethical use should come with an in-person heads-up to the people you frequently interact with. (Hello, fellow Verge writers and editors.)

Live Rewind, so far, has worked as described — with the heavy caveat that I’ve only tested it in my quiet home office with my spouse. Even so, it takes a hot second to learn the timing of a double press. My spouse noticed the audible chime signaling the feature is in use, though they didn’t notice the animation. I’ll have to see how this fares in louder environments. Siri accurately captured our attempts to get my cat to roll over, though in subsequent tests, it misheard a word or two.

I’m more hesitant to comment on Siri Recap. It’s not just because I haven’t had many organic, lengthy spoken conversations yet since downloading the beta. (Siri did not deem my brief conversation with my spouse as worthy enough for recapping.) But I won’t really get a sense for how this feature feels until I’ve tested it in a wide variety of scenarios. Will it work if I talk to myself aloud? How well does it filter out gossip? How will this change how people speak to me? That’ll be the true test of this feature and Apple’s bystander privacy claims.

My first Siri Recap was for an editorial planning meeting for a story I’m working on. It was decent at identifying different topics discussed, and I was impressed that it stripped out some sensitive information. Any outsider looking at these notes would be terribly confused. Ironically, it meant that this summary wasn’t the most useful for my job.

What I will say is that I’ve been testing the Amazon Bee Frontier for the past few weeks. In the little time I’ve spent with the watchOS 27.3 beta, the differences between Audio Intelligence and the Bee are very clear. The latter has more of what I’d call an AI-forward presence. Bee, for example, offers insights about the emotional tone of a conversation. I’ve also found that the AI can be a bit judgy about insights and takeaways. Live Rewind is just a straight transcript. Again, I’m still waiting on my first Siri Recap, but what Apple’s said publicly so far is that these are meant to be highly factual notes to jog a person’s memory. And, as far as I can tell, there is no commerce angle for Siri Recaps, whereas Bee has an Amazon integration that surfaces buying suggestions based on conversations.

In any case, I’ll be diving deep into these features in the days to come. Let us know in the comments what you’re most curious about.

신세계백화점의 VIP 전용 플랫폼 ‘더 쇼케이스’가 자동차와 맞춤형 주방 등 고가 상품으로 판매 영역을 넓히고 있다. 희소 상품에 시승과 개인별 상담 등을 결합하면서 올해 구매 객단가는 지난해의 5배 수준인 1억원을 넘어섰다.

4일 신세계백화점에 따르면 2024년 11월 출시한 더 쇼케이스는 백화점 앱에서 자동차와 주류, 전통공예품, 공간 컨설팅 등을 소개하는 서비스다. 매장에 진열된 상품을 구매하는 방식에서 나아가 고객의 취향에 맞는 상품과 경험을 제안하는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

올해 구매 객단가는 1억원을 넘어섰다. 이는 지난해(2000만원)의 5배 수준이다. 11억원이 넘는 슈퍼카와 평균 1억~3억원대 맞춤형 주방 등 특별한 경험에 투자를 아끼지 않는 VIP 소비 성향이 반영된 결과로 분석된다.

대표적으로 신세계는 올해 더 쇼케이스를 통해 람보르기니 서울과 협업한 지 3개월 만에 10대 이상을 판매했다. 관련 매출은 60억원을 돌파했다. 판매 차량에는 가격이 11억원을 넘는 플래그십 모델 ‘레부엘토’도 포함됐다. VIP 전용 시승과 프라이빗 행사를 더해 구매 과정 자체를 특별한 여정으로 구성한 것이 주효했다는 설명이다.

주거 공간을 개인 취향에 맞춰 꾸미려는 수요도 나타났다. 지난달 선보인 맞춤형 주방 브랜드 ‘쿠치넬라’에는 약 100건의 상담 문의가 접수됐다. 상담 고객 중 절반 가까이는 견적 금액이 3억원에 달했다.

쿠치넬라는 신세계까사의 고급 맞춤형 주방 브랜드다. 전담 디자이너가 고객과 일대일로 상담하며 사용 동선과 수납 방식을 파악하고 설계부터 시공까지 관리한다. 자재와 가전, 수납 시스템도 고객의 취향과 용도에 따라 구성한다.

신세계백화점은 이사 일정과 시공 기간에 따라 상담이 계약으로 이어지는 데 시간이 걸리는 점을 고려할 때, 연말까지 계약액이 수십억원에 이를 것으로 예상하고 있다.

한정판 주류와 전통공예품도 선보이고 있다. 지난 9월 산토리와 협업해 출시한 ‘치소 에디션’ 위스키는 판매 이틀 만에 준비 물량이 소진됐다. 국가유산청과의 업무협약을 바탕으로 칠장·나전장·낙화장 등 국가무형유산 전승자의 작품도 소개했다.

이성환 신세계백화점 영업전략담당 전무는 “VIP 고객들은 자신만의 취향과 라이프스타일을 반영한 상품과 차별화된 경험에 더욱 높은 가치를 두고 있다”며 “‘더 쇼케이스’를 통해 독보적인 상품 큐레이션과 개인별 맞춤형 서비스를 지속 확대하고, 기존 백화점의 상품과 서비스 차원을 넘어 VIP 고객들에게 보다 특별한 경험을 제시하는 플랫폼으로 발전시켜 나갈 것”이라고 말했다.

AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
items.summary: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer.
items.content:
Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported .

The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.)

The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted.

Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials.

Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon.

items.title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount
items.summary: The new ad placements could help Reddit squeeze more revenue from existing users as Google's AI search changes how people discover its content.
items.content:
Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it’s beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform.

“Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user’s search query,” Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. “This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time.”

The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for “espresso station” might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for “home office setup” could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs.

The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web’s landscape, and subsequently its reach.

Despite beating Wall Street’s estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company’s stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week , with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit’s declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google’s move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers’ websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google’s Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites.

Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter.

This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S.

The decision to limit its content to logged-in users serves multiple purposes — it protects Reddit’s site from unauthorized AI scraping, and it increases its value to advertisers. Logged-in users are worth more to advertisers because they provide additional signals about their interests and behavior, allowing for better-targeted, more profitable ads.

items.title: Ferrari’s controversial Luce EV is sold out for 2027
items.summary: The Luce, Ferrari's first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, is "fully allocated" through 2027, according to CEO Benedetto Vigna.
items.content:
The Luce, Ferrari’s first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, isn’t just selling. It’s selling out.

The five-seater EV designed by Jony Ive, Apple’s longtime design chief, was mocked and widely panned when it debuted in May, sending Ferrari’s stock price lower. But all that criticism hasn’t dampened demand, according to CEO Benedetto Vigna.

The 2027 production run of the Luce, which starts at about $615,000, is “fully allocated,” Vigna said Tuesday during the company’s third-quarter earnings call, meaning every car Ferrari plans to build next year already has a buyer. “If someone comes, he has to wait one year to get the cars,” Vigna added. The first deliveries of the Luce are expected to begin in the fourth quarter.

Just how many Luce cars that represents is unclear. Ferrari has never publicly disclosed how many Luce vehicles it plans to produce. Financial Times reported earlier this year, citing unnamed sources, that Ferrari planned to sell just under 500 units this year. The company’s longer-term target is to sell 2,500 units by 2030, or about 600 a year, according to Financial Times.

Speculation on who these buyers are — ahem, the founders of multibillion-dollar AI labs, perhaps? — will have to remain just that until Luces are spotted in the wild. Vigna wouldn’t provide a breakdown of who these Luce customers are, only noting it was a “good mix in terms of client, it is a good mix also in terms of geography.” He later added that there is no specific pattern or demographic of Luce buyers.

While Luce deliveries have yet to begin, Ferrari’s existing lineup and growing demand for personalized options helped fuel its financial performance in the third quarter . Revenue from customizations, which executives said accounted for more than 21% of revenue from cars and spare parts, helped boost profits. The company said deliveries of the F80, its limited-run hypercar , and customization reflect its clients’ “ever-deepening desire” to make each Ferrari uniquely their own. As a result, the company raised its full-year guidance, saying it now expects adjusted earnings of at least €3 billion ($3.36 billion), up from €2.97 billion.

Ferrari, which enjoys some of the highest profit margins in the auto industry, reported third-quarter revenue of €1.9 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, and net income of €431 million, up 13%. Operating profit was €563 million, for an operating margin of 29.7%, meaning the company kept roughly 30 cents of every dollar of revenue as profit from its core business.

items.title: Netflix’s new AI Discover tab helps you find something to watch based on your mood
items.summary: The first experimental feature under the tab will allow users to get recommendations based on what they're currently in the mood for.
items.content:
Netflix announced on Tuesday that it’s rolling out a new “AI Discover” tab where users will be able to experiment with new ways to find their next watch. The first experimental feature launching under the tab will allow users to get recommendations based on what they’re currently in the mood for.

Users can choose from curated themes featuring clips from shows and movies, based on their mood, viewing preferences, how much time they have, or what’s new and trending. Themes include “something light,” “scare me,” “family movie night,” “quick watches,” and more.

The addition of the new tab suggests that Netflix wants to make its growing library easier to navigate while shifting discovery away from an experience where users are endlessly scrolling through titles toward a more personalized and AI-powered experience.

Once users pick a theme, they’ll see matching recommendations. They also have the option to select more specific themes so they can keep searching until they find something they’re interested in, or choose the “something different” option to start over. Each title features a “Tune Your Recommendations” button beside “Play” and “My List” to allow users to save recommendations they like or exclude titles they don’t want suggested again.

“There’s more to enjoy and discover on Netflix than ever, but what sounds right for a quiet night in may look different for family movie night or a few spare minutes,” Netflix wrote in a blog post . “We’ve spent years refining how you discover, with recommendations tailored to your tastes, from what you Thumbs Up to what you add to ‘My List.’ Now, AI Discover joins the mix as a new way to explore.”

Netflix describes AI Discover as its “test kitchen,” where it will “try out new recipes for discovery.” The company says users’ feedback will help it decide which features to keep or improve before bringing them over to the main Netflix experience.

AI Discover is starting to roll out in the U.S. to users who use Netflix in English on supported TVs. The company plans to bring the new tab to additional users in the coming weeks.

If users have access to the new feature, they’ll see a “Discover” button with a red gem icon and a “New” label in the top navigation bar on their TV.

items.title: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
items.summary: Lawsuit calls Brave "supplier, dealer, and distributor" of stolen news content.
items.content:
The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies.

“Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere,” the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,” while “publishers have received nothing.”

The lawsuit said, “AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index,” and use content from the Brave index “to train their own AI models” and “to respond to specific user queries.” The NYT lawsuit points to Brave’s website , which says the Brave Search API is “used by some of the biggest names in AI, including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.”

The lawsuit accused Brave of all the major types of copyright infringement: direct infringement, contributory infringement, and vicarious infringement. The lawsuit claims Brave infringes copyrights directly by scraping articles for its search index, for its “Ask Brave” AI search feature, and for the Brave API that “serves as an illicit source of unlicensed copyrighted material, including Times journalism, to other AI companies.”

The NYT accused Brave of being “a contributory and vicarious infringer when it deliberately induces, facilitates, controls, and profits from its users’ and GenAI customers’ copying of the copyrighted content.” Finally, the lawsuit said Brave violated the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) by circumventing technological measures the NYT and other content owners use to restrict access to their articles.

“The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,” the lawsuit said. The browser “blocks advertising that would otherwise appear on The Times’s website, and instead shows its own ads, offering its users a cut of the revenue even as it deprives The Times of digital advertising revenue that helps it fund the expensive effort of producing journalism,” the lawsuit said.

When testing the Brave browser for Mac today, we found that the optional “paywall blocker” feature made it possible to read a paywalled New York Times article. The feature was enabled in the default settings and can be turned off.

The NYT asked for a permanent injunction to stop Brave from continuing the allegedly illegal conduct. The lawsuit seeks statutory damages, actual damages, restitution of profits derived from alleged copyright infringement, and “restitution and disgorgement of all revenue and profits Brave obtained through its ad-substitution scheme.”

A similar lawsuit was filed against Brave in the same court yesterday by the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel companies. We contacted Brave and will update this article if it provides a response.

Perplexity, which is not a defendant in the Brave lawsuit but is facing a different lawsuit filed by the NYT, accused the news organization of “disinformation” in a statement provided to Ars and other news outlets. Perplexity’s statement did not identify any specific inaccuracies in the lawsuit against Brave.

“The New York Times is overpaying its attorneys and underpaying its journalists. (Who could’ve easily identified the disinformation in this suit.),” Perplexity’s statement said.

The NYT sued Perplexity in December 2025, alleging that its AI tool gives users “outputs that are identical or substantially similar to” NYT articles, including “verbatim or near-verbatim reproductions, summaries, or abridgements of the original content.” Perplexity’s response to that lawsuit said its answer engine only fetches content from copyrighted articles in reply to user queries. Perplexity argued that “developing an AI tool that can allegedly automatically fetch and provide specific content in response to user requests based on its pre-configuration and access to materials available on the Internet” is not “volitional conduct.”

The NYT also sued OpenAI and Microsoft in December 2023 in a lawsuit alleging that OpenAI trains its AI with stolen news content. The lawsuit is heading toward a trial , with OpenAI arguing that its use of news articles is fair use under copyright law.

items.title: Buttons are back and storage is king when it comes to car interiors
items.summary: We talk with Nissan designer Hiren Patel about how vehicle interior designs are changing.
items.content:
As with interior design for houses, interior design for vehicles is also subject to fashion trends. And like any fashion trend, even the best ideas can become stale and played out with overuse. Some ideas weren’t the best, either, like demonstrably worse human-machine interfaces that add to driver distraction; yet, they still proliferated throughout the industry and across the cars offered for sale. But the good news is that the pushback seems to be working.

“When the trend of the Piano Black and the switchless interior was happening, it was during a time when designers and companies and engineers and everybody were thinking that, ‘Hey, we can just get rid of all these switches on the interior. We can put it all in the software. It’ll save money. It’ll save us tooling up all these extra parts for unique cars and all this stuff and make the interior more like a software experience.’ And it was done with those intentions,” said Hiren Patel, senior design manager at Nissan.

That resulted in cars with minimalist interiors that looked good in the dealership. But people drive their cars on roads; they don’t just sit inside them, parked inside a dealership. “So lots of people were complaining about it and saying, ‘Hey, it takes my eyes off the road to change the temperature or to adjust my seat or do whatever.’ It’s not as easy as doing something on your phone where it’s just right at your fingertips and intuitive,” Patel said.

In part, blame the increasing complexity of modern cars, which have multiple subsystems that need to be controlled. “It’s really like I’ve got to go in all these menus and do stuff, and all the car companies have a different way of doing it, too. So maybe nobody’s really figured out a great way of doing it.”

Most recently, Patel was responsible for the new Rogue , Nissan’s bestselling family SUV. And its interior is a good one. Less minimalist than the all-electric Ariya, the new Rogue Hybrid has buttons and switches for most of its controls and a useful amount of storage built into the interior. Yet it’s not a boring design—the seats are a standout, taking inspiration from puffer jackets. And no, there’s no Piano Black in sight.

“People want easy, intuitive controls,” Patel said. “They want wireless charging. They want surfaces that are easy to manage and clean, keep clean and clutter-free, and they want lots of places to store things. Oh, and the last thing is, they want easy access.” So the new Rogue’s rear doors were engineered to open to 90˚ to make it easier to put in a kid’s car seat or help an elderly parent into the back. That would be less of a priority for a sedan being marketed at a more image-conscious customer, but vitally important for this segment.

“The target customer for this product… they have families and they have a lot of stuff. So you’ll notice that you open the door, and immediately there’s places to put stuff,” Patel said.

Utilitarian need not mean prosaic, however. As designers since the Bauhaus movement have proved, “everyday” doesn’t have to be ordinary. Patel shared that sentiment. “One of the exciting things and one of the really big challenging things of doing a car or doing design for a product that is a usable everyday product is when you can make that product beautiful,” he said. “There’s so much more that goes into our everyday usable products in terms of cost, engineering, usability, feasibility, everything. And then on top of that, we’re struggling and really trying our best to fight for every little millimeter that we can get that we feel is important to making sure that that product is appealing from a visual standpoint.”

Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike is buying two AI security companies that expand its products to more broadly monitor, test, and cover AI models and agents, as companies across industries start rolling out AI agents and models wholesale.

CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI , which makes observability software for monitoring AI agents inside enterprises, and Dreadnode , which helps companies automate security testing specifically aimed at detecting flaws in AI models, apps and agents before they are set live.

The company is paying around $400 million for Fiddler AI, and about $95 million for Dreadnode, according to The Wall Street Journal .

The deals are happening at a time of significant upheaval in the cybersecurity space, especially as companies’ policies and processes lag behind AI adoption within their walls. Teams and individual employees alike are experimenting with AI tools, automating workflows, vibe-coding custom apps, and deploying armies of AI agents to do their bidding, which is understandably causing headaches for security teams.

CrowdStrike, whose products are used widely across enterprises and governments, is clearly trying to leverage its already significant heft and presence to capture a share of this quickly burgeoning market . It’s not alone, of course, as we’ve already seen several startups and cybersecurity vendors raising dozens of millions in funding to solve issues for companies, though most of these approaches are essentially based on the conviction that existing security software isn’t enough to monitor and control AI tools, connectors, or usage.

The company has itself been building detection and response controls , dubbed Falcon Guardian, to help companies see and understand what agents are doing on their devices, and these acquisitions seem to further flesh out its offerings.

Fiddler AI is going to be part of CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform as Falcon Observe, where it’ll ostensibly help the company’s clients evaluate agents before they’re deployed, understand their actions, and monitor what they do, and feed that information as telemetry into the broader platform. Dreadnode, meanwhile, will be integrated into the Falcon Guardian product , to which the startup’s software will feed its testing results as security policy recommendations.

Founded in 2018, Fiddler AI has raised a total of about $99 million to date, according to PitchBook. Dreadnode, founded in 2023, has raised $14 million so far.

items.title: Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too
items.summary: Google will offer schools AI tools that purportedly don't give away the answers.
items.content:
While Google is trying to move beyond Chromebooks , the ubiquity of these devices has made the company’s education products huge in schools. Now, Google says it will let educators choose whether to allow its AI tools in the classroom. However, blocking AI tools also means giving up search, leaving schools with a difficult decision.

Google’s new overarching approach to AI in K-12 classrooms sounds good on the surface. After consulting educators, researchers, and lawmakers, Google has decided that schools using its education products will be opted out of AI tools by default. It will be up to administrators to manually enable them when these changes roll out in the coming months.

When you look at what Google considers to be an AI tool, the nature of the Faustian bargain becomes clear. The affected products are Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search . There’s no picking and choosing—you either allow all the AI or none of it.

This is actually consistent with Google’s approach in the consumer space. Google executives have said in no uncertain terms that Google Search is AI search . Most searches now provide an AI Overview at the top, and the company is constantly coming up with new ways to nudge people toward the conversational AI Mode chatbot function. Google sees this as the future.

In a statement to The New York Times , Google education VP Chris Phillips reiterated this approach to web search. “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” he said, adding that if a school chooses not to enable AI, the students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

Google could make a version of search for schools that doesn’t have AI tools, but it’s not doing that. Instead, it’s creating two different versions of AI in search. When schools enable AI for student accounts, they’ll have two options: the standard Gemini-based AI and the new “Guided Learning” version. The latter, available in Classroom as well as search, is supposed to provide one-on-one tutoring and assistance without giving away all the answers. Google notes all of its generative AI products can make “mistakes,” though, so it may not be difficult to talk the chatbot into doing your homework.

Google is betting that schools won’t want to give up Google Search and will therefore accept AI tools. This will expose students to AI early and often, possibly changing the way they interact with technology. Schools that don’t like Google’s approach could switch to alternatives like DuckDuckGo, which lets you disable AI features. But will Google’s new Guided Learning be enough to assuage their concerns?

items.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.summary: Article URL: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/3/qwen-can-interpret-model-weights/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50355251 Points: 506 # Comments: 157
items.content:
Yesterday’s hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper (OK, the authors classify is as a “blog post”, but it’s paper-shaped) found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model—literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers. I’ve been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I’m delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well!

Here’s the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights:

Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do . And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.

Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights . With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x.

All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming .

The paper combines two topics that I think deserve to be treated separately. The first is what models can do with raw weights without running tools or executing code. The second explores how well models, once armed with code, can run operations to update and improve other models.

spaCy author Matthew Honnibal called the paper misleading for conflating the two, and Sean Goedecke deconstructed the Qwen3.5-0.8B update example as taking the same steps that a human ML researcher would use.

I’m going to focus on the no-tools question, which I think is the more interesting of the two.

The paper presents the first question as Can LLMs understand model behaviors from weights? They trained four neural networks to play simplified 10x10 grid versions of four classic computer games—Breakout, Pong, Pac-Man, and Freeway (I had to look that one up , it’s an Atari 2600 game from 1981). Then they fed those weights (as floating point numbers) to an LLM along with the following question:

The weights below belong to one policy network that was trained with reinforcement learning to play a game on this grid. Which game was it trained on? Work from the weights. You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run. This is a single response.

The GitHub repository that accompanies the paper is RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs . The exp1_which_game folder contains the prompts they used, with weights for the four games:

I checked and, aside from the weights, each prompt is identical to the others.

The prompts on GitHub are self-contained. My LLM tool has a -f/--fragment option which can be passed the URL to a text file to use as a prompt, which means I can run any of the above like this:

This example requires the llm-openrouter plugin installed, and runs the Breakout prompt against Kimi K3.1 Pro via OpenRouter. Here’s what I got back from Kimi K3.1 Pro , which successfully guessed Breakout after 9m 41s and 19,493 reasoning tokens.

But how about Qwen 3.8 27B ? That’s still my favorite model to run on my own laptop—it’s just 17GB (I use this version ) and somehow feels close to the leading proprietary models of 2025.

(I had to bump the timeout up using an environment variable, see this issue .)

After 46m 12s and 43,506 reasoning tokens, Qwen on my laptop returned a response that ended like this (here’s the reasoning trace ):

Game: A simplified Pac-Man-style gridworld: an agent moves through a fixed 8x8 maze with central and corner wall blocks, moving objects/ghosts, and reward targets/pellets.

Description: The agent navigates a fixed maze-like 8x8 board, using current agent/moving-object/previous-frame cues to move through corridors, collect reward-target cells, and avoid moving objects or hazards.

This is impressive. I tried it on two of the other games as well. It identified Pong ( reasoning ) in 1h 4m 54s:

Pong — specifically a Pong-like paddle/ball game where the agent controls a vertical paddle on the right side and must move up/down to intercept or return a moving ball/reward object.

The agent moves a right-side paddle vertically to hit or catch a moving ball-like reward target moving across the 8×8 field, while a left-side moving object/opponent and wall borders define the play; reward is obtained by successfully intercepting/returning/scoring the ball, and missing or failing to hit it is penalized.

And Breakout ( reasoning ) in 52m 25s:

Description: The agent is a paddle on the bottom row and moves left/right to keep a ball in play; the ball moves around the upper grid, and bricks/reward targets in the top rows give reward when hit, while missing the ball/hitting the bottom wall ends the episode or gives penalty.
